note: AT&T's modeled ways and ranking, exported from the storefront prototype. Treat as a starting point for the team's option list, not a source.

ways.title: Bring your own port
ways.line: Your Direct Connect, ExpressRoute or Interconnect, carried on the AT&T network. NetBond Advanced as it runs today.
ways.setupWords: Guided reconfig · <15 min on AT&T's side; the first time needs your cloud gateway

youDo.words: Accept the connection, attach your cloud gateway, confirm BGP

ways.title: AT&T provides the port
ways.line: AT&T orders the cloud's Direct Connect or ExpressRoute and holds it. One order, one bill.
ways.setupWords: Guided reconfig · <15 min on AT&T's side

youDo.words: Accept the hosted connection, attach your cloud gateway, confirm BGP

ways.title: Hosted peering
ways.line: AT&T's hub VPC or VNet, with the vSRX in path, peered to yours. L3 to L7 policy in AT&T's hub.
ways.setupWords: Click + approve · 15-30 min, a proof-of-concept target

youDo.words: Accept the peering and add one route

ways.title: Transit gateway
ways.line: AT&T runs a transit gateway in its hub and shares it; your VPCs attach. Transitive routing, central inspection.
ways.setupWords: Click + approve · 30-60 min, a proof-of-concept target

youDo.words: Accept the share, attach your VPC and update its route table

ways.title: Cloud WAN
ways.line: AT&T runs the core network across regions; your VPC attaches to its edge and joins a segment.
ways.setupWords: Guided reconfig · 1-2 hrs, a proof-of-concept target

youDo.words: Attach your VPC to the edge and join a segment

ways.title: PrivateLink
ways.line: AT&T publishes each service; you create one private endpoint per service. Overlapping CIDRs are fine.
ways.setupWords: Click + approve · 15-30 min each, a proof-of-concept target

youDo.words: Create an endpoint per service, approve it, set up DNS

options.label: Critical
options.words: Business critical: zone-redundant, SLA-backed, two paths

options.label: Production
options.words: Production: the deck's weights as they stand

options.label: Lab
options.words: A lab: cost and speed first; one zone is fine

options.label: Priority
options.words: Priority traffic: deterministic latency, held to an SLO

options.label: Standard
options.words: Standard traffic: best path, no SLO of its own

options.label: Private
options.words: A private path: never the public internet, route policy at L3

options.label: Inspected
options.words: Inspected in path: L3 to L7 on the vSRX in AT&T's hub

options.label: Per service
options.words: Per service: expose named services only, no routed reach

options.label: Your BGP
options.words: You peer BGP with AT&T, as your sites already do: routed both ways

options.label: AT&T's hub
options.words: AT&T runs the routing in its hub; no gateway in your VPC

options.label: Transitive
options.words: Many VPCs reach each other through one hub

rules.removes: One zone only: an outage takes it down
No inspection in path: L3 route policy only
Routed, not per service: reaches the whole VPC

rules.prefers: a way where you run BGP yourself

rules.removes: You run the gateway: and BGP, in your VPC
Not transitive: one peering per VPC

ranking: Each answer adds or removes weight on the five criteria (never below 5, scaled to 100). A way scores each criterion 1 to 5; the weighted sum out of 100, plus 5 for each soft preference it meets, is its score. A hard rule a way breaks counts as a miss. Ways sort by fewest misses, then score, then the cheaper monthly.
